Title: T-MAP: Red-Teaming LLM Agents with Trajectory-aware Evolutionary Search
Abstract: While prior red-teaming efforts have focused on eliciting harmful text outputs from large language models (LLMs), such approaches fail to capture agent-specific vulnerabilities that emerge through multi-step tool execution, particularly in rapidly growing ecosystems such as the Model Context Protocol (MCP).To address this gap, we propose a trajectory-aware evolutionary search method, T-MAP, which leverages execution trajectories to guide the discovery of adversarial prompts.Our approach enables the automatic generation of attacks that not only bypass safety guardrails but also reliably realize harmful objectives through actual tool interactions.Empirical evaluations across diverse MCP environments demonstrate that T-MAP substantially outperforms baselines in attack realization rate (ARR) and remains effective against frontier models, including GPT-5.2,Gemini-3-Pro, Qwen3.5, and GLM-5, thereby revealing previously underexplored vulnerabilities in autonomous LLM agents.
Major_Contribution_Result: T-MAP is a trajectory-aware MAP-Elites evolutionary search for red-teaming MCP-integrated LLM agents, measuring Attack Realization Rate (ARR) via actual tool execution rather than harmful text alone. Across five MCP environments it reports the highest ARR in each and an average ARR of 57.8%, outperforming baselines such as IR (e.g., ARR 3.1%–40.6% across environments) and achieving higher realized-attack diversity (|HL3|=21.80 vs 12.80 for SE). Authors state effectiveness against frontier models including GPT-5.2, Gemini-3-Pro, Qwen3.5, and GLM-5.
Research_Limitations_Challenges: Evaluation covers five MCP servers; broader agent environments remain future work. Experiments are sandboxed, whereas real deployments may add permission checks, user confirmation, validation, and sandboxing that could reduce practical ARR. The framework relies on DeepSeek-V3.2 as attacker, whose weaker safety alignment aids prompt generation; effectiveness may shift as attacker alignment improves.
Critics: T-MAP is an offensive search method scored by tool-realized harm in controlled MCP sandboxes, not a defensive benchmark comparison. ARR numbers are relative to the authors' evolutionary baselines and five servers, so they should not be extrapolated as universal agent vulnerability rates. Useful for trajectory-aware MCP red-teaming evaluation methodology.
